fidelityReview.scope: Restored Wannsee villa exterior: hipped tiled roof with eyebrow dormer, columned street facade, lake-facing pediment and loggia, shutters and raised terrace. Exclude the wider garden and separate garden house.
fidelityReview.notes: Full restored villa exterior accepted at the agreed approximate medium-fi scope. The exact1518×1177public-domain1918MeinHausinWannsee painting already published on Qualla was inspected individually first. It supports the lake facade, paired storeys, central tall openings/pilasters, raised terrace and left loggia. Berlin heritage record09075511 independently identifies the broad two-storey plaster body, natural-stone base, hipped roof, large street eyebrow dormer, monumental Ionic columns, central lake pediment over three window axes and open left lake loggia. Restoring architects Nedelykov/Moreira independently describe the final simple hipped roof, seven lake-facing window axes, tall garden doors, sand-coloured rough plaster, pale sandstone bands/frames, shell-limestone details and green timber shutters. Museum restoration history identifies the2003–06restored building as the same historic architecture. Existing geometry agrees with those controls and the native mapped envelope. No new geometry was required. Exact roof pitch/eyebrow curve, colours, side openings, terrace depth, small side entrance/pergola and capital/railing profiles remain bounded medium-fi approximations; the artwork is not a photograph or measured elevation. Full original main-villa/upper-terrace scope retained; wider garden, separate garden house, interiors, furniture and vegetation excluded. Native Berlin DGM1 ground and placement remain unchanged. No reference pixels embedded.
